newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up, trade wary of ringgit.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up, trade wary of ringgit.

text.p: Malaysia's rubber market closed higher on Wednesday but there were hardly reports of trade, with buyers remaining wary of a weak ringgit.
"They are being very careful, the buyers," said a trader.
"Unless they are desperate for stocks, which are doubtful, they can wait for prices to fall as the ringgit looks like it'll strengthen again," said the trader.
Malaysia's central Bank Negara checked dollar/ringgit rates at 2.57 on Wednesday and the ringgit closed at 2.5580 in Kuala Lumpur.
The Malaysian currency has lost more than 600 points in the last week.
Dealers said trading was also cautious ahead of a holiday in Kuala Lumpur. The Malaysian rubber market will be closed on Thursday for a Moslem holiday.
At the close, the August buyer price for the RSS1 was 234 Malaysia/Singapore cents (91 U.S. cents), up three cents from Tuesday. The SMR20 for August buyer stood at 236 cents, up 1.50 cents.
Traders quoted the SMR20 at 243/244 cents, the SMR10 at 242, SMR5 at 249, SMR CV at 296, SMR L at 278, and drum latex at 194.
The INRO's five-day average price strengthened at 183.01 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg on July 15, compared to 182.27 on July 14. The daily indicator rose to 185.51 from 183.92 previously.
Malaysian-based shipping brokers quoted freight rates for rubber from Malaysia to Rotterdam at $700 per 20-ft container, and $1,400 per 40-ft container.
